title: Power Automate - Simply Explained
description:
Repetitive tasks like copying data, forwarding approvals and sending the same emails eat hours every week. This beginner-friendly episode explains Power Automate in plain English for Microsoft 365 users, covering triggers, actions, connectors, cloud and desktop flows, and how to build your first flow in minutes without code.
In this episode
00:00 – What Power Automate is00:37 – The problem Power Automate solves01:53 – Trigger plus action03:27 – The three types of flows05:01 – Connectors06:35 – Cloud flows vs. desktop flows09:57 – Real-world examples11:31 – Your first flow in five minutes
Key takeaways
Every Power Automate flow is a trigger plus one or more actions, and automated, instant and scheduled flows differ only in how the trigger fires.Hundreds of pre-built connectors let flows link Microsoft 365 apps like SharePoint, Teams and Outlook with third-party services, and custom connectors cover any system with an API.Cloud flows run on Microsoft's servers for modern services, while desktop flows use RPA to drive legacy applications by mouse and keyboard.
Worth quoting
“Most people think power automate is complicated, but strip away all the marketing and technical jargon and it's really just when this happens, do that.” – Mirko Peters (03:14)
“The core engine is exactly the same for all three types. The only real difference is the trigger. Automated flows use event triggers. Instant flows use manual triggers. Scheduled flows use time triggers” – Mirko Peters (04:44)
